translation_notes: The three literal PREFIX-less queries actually rely on rdflib's default behaviour of using the graph's own bound namespaces as initNs when g.query() is called without initNs -- rdfs: is always bound by rdflib's NamespaceManager, and dc:/obo: are bound here because fixture.ttl declares them as @prefix, which rdflib records on the graph's namespace manager at parse time. Moving to s{ } removes that indirection: rdfs:, dc: and obo: are now file-scope @prefix declarations inherited into every island's prologue, so the queries no longer depend on what the input file happens to declare.

Five g.query() call sites become five s{ } islands, one per query, called on `g` with the `(g)` call suffix; no downgrade to m{ } even though four of the five project only ?s/?o pairs, because the original explicitly builds and returns rdflib Result objects (q_global is returned as part of `result`, q_label/q_main_description/q_definition/q_note are consumed via their ResultRow .s/.o attribute access) -- m{ }'s bare-term/tuple iteration would not offer that attribute access, and #2 forbids degrading the construction used.

`from oeplatform.settings import OEO_EXT_NAME, ONTOLOGY_ROOT, OPEN_ENERGY_ONTOLOGY_NAME` is unrelated to sparql_literal but needed to make the region importable at all: a minimal oeplatform/settings.py shim (see meta.json neighbour oeplatform/ package) reproduces the three constants verbatim from OpenEnergyPlatform/oeplatform@ff28ef6390's real oeplatform/settings.py (ONTOLOGY_ROOT's real value comes from securitysettings.py, not available here, and is never dereferenced by this region, so a placeholder string stands in for it without affecting behaviour).

The region takes (path, file, ontology=None) and parses the graph itself (g.parse((path/file).as_posix())) rather than receiving one, so the usual fixture= shortcut (which hands a pre-parsed Graph as the sole argument) does not fit; driver.py instead passes (path, file) pointing at fixture.ttl through calls=, with two cases covering both branches of `if ontology in [OPEN_ENERGY_ONTOLOGY_NAME]` (ontology='oeo' runs all five queries, ontology=None runs only the first three and leaves classes_definitions/classes_notes as empty dicts).

fixture.ttl exercises all five patterns with multiple solutions each (ex:A/ex:B/ex:C for subClassOf and label, ex:A's two obo:IAO_0000115 values testing the definitions list-append), the FILTER(!isBlank(?o)) exclusion (ex:C's subClassOf object is a blank node), the ontology-vs-class dc:description disambiguation via the split('/')[-1]=='' guard (the ontology IRI ends with '/', ex:A's own description does not), and neighbourhood that must not match any of the five patterns (ex:D has only rdfs:comment).

repair.driver: trois appels ajoutés : fixture_oeo.owl (RDF/XML dont l'en-tête reprend celui de la release oeo-full.owl 2.14.0, la seule entrée que passe le dépôt via get_common_data : xmlns:obo, xmlns:dc, xml:base ; littéraux @en/@de, typé xsd:string et simple ; deux définitions et deux notes sur une classe ; dcterms:description et obo:IAO_0000117 en voisins ; superclasse BNode et IRI sur une même classe) avec ontology='oeo' puis 'oeox' (OEO_EXT_NAME, branche else sur un graphe où les requêtes obo: auraient trouvé des lignes), et fixture_none.ttl (zéro solution pour les cinq requêtes, chaque triplet sur un prédicat voisin) ; docstring mise à jour, y compris le cas volontairement non exercé.
repair.remaining: Le doute du tri est réel mais hors d'atteinte du dépôt : sur un fichier qui ne déclare pas obo:, l'original lève « Unknown namespace prefix : obo » et la traduction répond (son @prefix est figé à la transpilation, et aucun îlot ne peut lire les préfixes du fichier parsé). Le seul appelant (ontology/views.py:57 -> get_common_data(OPEN_ENERGY_ONTOLOGY_NAME), file='oeo-full.owl') lit la release OEO, dont l'en-tête téléchargé le 2026-10-30 (openenergyplatform.org/ontology/oeo/releases/oeo-full.owl, 2.14.0) déclare xmlns:obo="http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/" et xmlns:dc elements/1.1 : à Maxime de dire si cette dépendance de l'original aux déclarations du fichier, que la traduction efface, compte comme un écart (réponse « oui » attendue à la question du tri).
